attributes.grant-summary: ARC Research Hub for Productivity Acceleration in Construction Ecosystems. This research hub aims to transform construction productivity, cut waste/emission, and improve safety via resource-efficient and intelligent methods across design, manufacturing, site delivery, and operations. It is significant because Australia faces rising costs, labour shortages, approval delays, and the need to decarbonise buildings/infrastructure. Expected outcomes include new design tools, automated compliance and planning, human-robot worksites, low-carbon materials with traceability, and practical standards and training. Benefits are faster, safer, lower cost delivery and a more skilled workforce. Impact will be measurable reductions in time, cost, and emissions on real projects, supporting national housing and infrastructure needs.

attributes.national-interest-test-statement: In Australia productivity in the construction sector has been declining for decades, while demand for housing and infrastructure is increasing. Most of the sector has not adopted technological innovations, despite a shrinking labour force and lack of skilled workers. This sector has large carbon and waste footprints that are impeding our sustainable and net-zero goals. The ARC Research Hub for Productivity Acceleration in Construction Ecosystems connects engineers, architects and IT scientists with industry, government and peak bodies across Australia to address productivity along the entire construction lifecycle. It will develop building construction technologies, intelligent automation and decision support systems to link design with delivery, asset management and end-of-life using advances in digitalisation, robotics, and AI. It will increase adoption of these innovations and low-carbon solutions through workforce transformation and policy support. Faster, better and cleaner advances in on-site and off-site construction will improve sector productivity, safety, sustainability, efficiency and building maintenance. Worth 7% of Australia’s GDP, improvements in this sector will have enormous economic, commercial, environmental and social benefits, helping address the housing crisis. Hub results, tools, practices and policy briefs will be shared with industry and government via industry-led outreach programs and to the public via social and traditional media.

attributes.grant-summary: ARC Research Hub for Next-Gen Tropical Aquaculture. The ARC ITRH for Next-Gen Tropical Aquaculture will tackle the biological challenges limiting sustainable tropical aquaculture production of seafood, such as variable growth, feed efficiency, stress, and disease. Current aquaculture systems rely on delayed or incomplete biological data, leaving issues poorly managed. By applying sensors, artificial intelligence, automation, and genomics, the Hub will enable real-time monitoring and prediction of biological performance. This will support better breeding, feeding, and health management, reducing costs and risks, improving animal welfare, and lowering environmental impacts. The Hub will strengthen northern Australia’s economy and establish the nation as a leader in sustainable aquaculture.

attributes.national-interest-test-statement:
Australia’s aquaculture industry is critical for future food security, regional economies, & export competitiveness. This project will be focused on aquaculture of tropical species, such as barramundi, grouper, prawns, crayfish & pearls, which currently have an annual value of $372M that is expected to grow to $1.34B by 2030. Scientific & commercialisation outcomes of the project will be also applicable to other aquaculture industries in Australia & globally. Our industry partners estimate that the successful realization of the research objectives will result in savings to the northern Australian aquaculture of up to $5M annually. 

The ARC Hub for Next-Gen Tropical Aquaculture will deliver the knowledge & tools needed to manage biological processes in real time, enabling proactive decisions that improve breeding, feeding, health, & marine environment management. This will reduce operational risks, cut waste, & enhance environmental resilience, directly benefiting industry & regional communities in northern Australia.

Nationally, the Hub aligns with government priorities in food security & environmental sustainability. Internationally, it positions Australia as a trusted leader in aquaculture innovation, opening opportunities for technology export & regional collaboration. By training the next generation of specialists, the Hub will build sovereign capability to produce high-quality seafood & to support industry growth, resilience, & competitiveness for decades to come.

attributes.grant-summary: ARC Research Hub for Quantum Safety Testing. Securing current IT systems from future quantum computing innovations that can easily decrypt sensitive data is critical for future-proofing and transforming Australia’s technology ecosystem to become a global leader in systems migration and quantum-resilient technologies. This research hub aims to develop automated security testing and certifications enabling critical infrastructure cybersecurity without increased burden. The expected outcomes are more secure ecosystems reducing cyberattack costs, estimated at $33 billion. The benefit is economic opportunity that is predicted to generate novel quantum safety testing and certifications enabling Australia to become a global leader in the automated testing industry valued at $45.6 billion.

attributes.national-interest-test-statement: Most governments including the Australian Government are expecting that, by 2030, quantum computing will create vulnerabilities in existing security algorithms exposing industries to cyber risk at scale. However, securing and migrating industries to be quantum-resilient can be time-consuming and burdensome but is a necessary step to protect data and revenue. Our industry research hub will develop quantum-resilient automated testing and certification equipping Australian organisations with the ability to efficiently secure their data against future quantum computing-enabled threats while also providing Australia with an edge in the global automated testing industry. Research outcomes from this hub will accelerate the cyber security maturity of Australian companies and critical infrastructure (e.g., finance, data centres) future-proofing them against future quantum computing cyber threats. Our partners span the full range of research translation, from quantum computing and cyber security researchers through to end-users and partners, ensuring that developed testing and certification solutions can be quickly deployed and taken up by industry and society delivering world-leading quantum security and resilience.

attributes.grant-summary: ARC Training Centre for Sustainable Ground Stabilisation Technologies towards a Net-Zero Future for Strategic Infrastructure (ITTC-GeoStab). This Training Centre (ITTC-GeoStab) aims to transform infrastructure sector knowhow and practice through innovative sustainable ground stabilisation technologies that are core to the design and construction of resilient civil infrastructure. By delivering rigorous training of industry-focused researchers and professionals, the Centre will develop a highly skilled, industry-ready workforce alongside technological breakthrough. This dual focus will accelerate the shift to low-carbon, energy-efficient ground-stabilisation processes. The resulting R&D outputs will strengthen industry tools and capabilities to help Australia meet its emissions-reduction targets, while delivering substantial economic, environmental, and societal benefits.

attributes.national-interest-test-statement:
Australia’s infrastructure sector must urgently decarbonise to meet the national Net Zero 2050 targets without compromising safety, durability or cost-effectiveness. ITTC-GeoStab will address this challenge by advancing sustainable ground stabilisation technologies to integrate low-carbon, energy-efficient and circular-economy practices. By transforming waste materials such as tyres, glass, plastics and mining byproducts into high-performance construction resources, the research will reduce landfill waste and embodied carbon, while creating new industrial value chains.
The research will generate clear national benefits by lowering construction and maintenance costs and extending the service life of roads, railways, and ports amid increasing climatic and loading conditions. Environmentally, the Centre will drive significant emissions reductions in civil work, while advancing sustainable resource use. It will further enhance safety, reliability, and connectivity across vital transport networks underpinning the nation’s economic resilience.
ITTC-GeoStab will drive rapid uptake of its innovations through close collaboration with industry, government, and professional bodies, and the tangible outcomes will be embedded in technical standards and design guides. Through targeted training programs and workshops, the Centre will help build a highly skilled, carbon-literate workforce, positioning Australia as a global leader in sustainable geoengineering and resilient infrastructure.

attributes.grant-summary: ARC Training Centre in Engineering Biology for Sustainable Materials. This Centre will address Australia’s urgent need for a sustainable materials workforce. This Centre will use Engineering Biology; a technology that programs microbes to build new materials and reduce petrochemical use. This Centre will unite universities with industry, government and investment partners. Researchers will be trained in science, regulation, business and policy to ensure innovations are market-ready. This Centre will transform bio-based manufacturing via interdisciplinary approaches aligned with national priorities. Outcomes include new biomaterials and industry-ready researchers. Benefits include an accelerated domestic bioeconomy, new future jobs and a workforce strengthening Australia’s sovereign biomanufacturing capacity.

attributes.national-interest-test-statement:
Australia’s transition toward a circular economy demands an immediate, systemic shift away from petrochemical dependence toward sustainable materials. The ARC Training Centre for Engineering Biology for Sustainable Materials (EBSM) addresses this national challenge by building the capability to design and produce new bioderived materials made using safe, renewable biological processes. The EBSM will combine expertise across microbiology, materials science, chemistry, economics and the humanities to engineer microbes and proteins for sustainable production of novel biomaterials.
This research will benefit Australians economically by strengthening advanced manufacturing, creating skilled jobs, and enabling local companies to compete in a global bio-based materials market. Environmentally, it supports national decarbonisation efforts by enabling low-carbon, biodegradable materials that reduce waste and pollution. Socially, it promotes responsible and transparent innovation through community engagement and clear regulatory guidance for new products.
To maximise adoption beyond academia, the EBSM will work closely with our innovative small business partners to train a specialised workforce with cross disciplinary expertise, and directly catalyse Australia’s shift toward a resilient, high-value economy.

attributes.grant-summary: ARC Training Centre for Advancing Capability in Biopesticides for Crops. The Adv-BioCrop Centre aims to address critical gaps in the capability, regulation and safe use of biopesticides. In doing so, the Centre will herald a transformative on-the-ground shift in how pests and diseases are managed in Australian agriculture through targeted training and industry capacity building rooted by strategic and applied research. While delivering on the urgent need for skilled professionals, the Centre will produce regulatory protocols reducing biopesticide product registration timelines by 30-50%; validated biological solutions to protect crop value; and technical guidelines supporting farmer adoption. Benefits include preserved Australian access to global markets, new commercial products, healthier foods and environment.

attributes.national-interest-test-statement: Agriculture is an economic cornerstone in Australia, generating $71.5B in annual exports. Around 73% of production is currently enabled by crop protection products (mostly chemical)—increasing 53% in just 5 years. Climate change is expected to exacerbate and intensify threats, while widespread pesticide resistance is rendering current products obsolete and regulatory withdrawal of key chemical actives is closing off traditional solutions. International markets, which absorb over 70% of Australia's agriculture products, are also tightening pesticide restrictions. Without a fundamental shift in crop protection approach—from chemical to biological—Australia will face significant productivity losses, and risks ceding $3B in export markets to competitors. The Adv-BioCrop Centre amasses 21 strategic R&D, government and commercial partners to co-develop and directly integrate cutting-edge research that characterises novel biocontrol agents, develops and commercialises biopesticides, and produces highly skilled personnel, tools and validated biological crop protection approaches. This builds critical national capability for accelerated transformation in insect pest and disease management in Australian agriculture and more deeply seeds Australia in the global biopesticide market, projected to reach $10.9B by 2027. Australians will benefit from reduced pesticide residues in food and water, improved occupational safety for agricultural workers, and less polluted natural environments.

attributes.grant-summary:
ARC Training Centre for Digital Architectural Translation: Accelerating Circularity Adoption. The Centre will generate specialised workforce capacity, platforms, practices and processes to accelerate the Australian architectural sector’s role in achieving national circularity targets. It will do this by leveraging advanced architectural, computational, and technical approaches to translate circularity insights into actionable forms (software, workflows, augmented intelligence and demonstrator projects) to drive real-world impacts.
Through its program of industry-embedded PhDs, national and international placements, industry-facing short courses, and post-doctoral projects, the Centre co-develops with industry the change agents needed to transform the architectural sector’s capability to meet our nation’s urgent circularity needs.

attributes.national-interest-test-statement:
The Australian Government’s Circular Economy Framework (2024) identifies the built environment as a priority for urgent transformation due to its high material use and waste generation. A central focus is investment in “design for circularity” as a key enabler for meeting national targets. Architects can drive this shift, as their decisions shape every stage of a building’s life. Yet they lack effective ways to translate Australia’s world-leading circular-economy research into practical design and construction methods.

The ARC Training Centre for Digital Architectural Translation: Accelerating Circularity Adoption will bridge this gap by turning theory into practice. It will deliver innovative training and create new software tools, workflows, and design-to-manufacturing processes to help architects reduce waste, reuse materials, support adaptation and refurbishment, and design for modularity and disassembly. Its industry-embedded postgraduates, targeted short courses, and practical solutions will help position the built environment as a central driver of Australia’s transition to a sustainable circular economy. These efforts are crucial in reducing the 29 Mt of construction waste produced each year in Australia.

The Centre’s aims and scope directly align with the National Reconstruction Fund’s ‘Enabling Capabilities’ and ‘Renewables and Low-Emissions Technologies’ priorities, as well as with the National Science and Research Priority’ Transitioning to a Net Zero Future’.

attributes.grant-summary: ARC Research Hub for Safe and Ethical Humanoid Robot Implementation and Adoption. This project aims to ensure the safe and ethical use of humanoid robots in Australia’s care, construction, and manufacturing industries. It will bring researchers and industry together to test how these robots can support workers, reduce injury and labour shortages, and improve wellbeing and productivity. The intended outcome is practical guidance, standards, and design tools that make humanoids safe, trusted and beneficial in real workplaces. The expected benefits include stronger national capability, better workforce outcomes, and responsible adoption of emerging robotics technologies that enhance rather than replace human work.

attributes.national-interest-test-statement:
This project supports Australia’s people and economy by preparing the nation for the safe, ethical and productive adoption of humanoid robots across critical industries, including care, construction and manufacturing. These sectors face growing workforce shortages, safety risks and productivity pressures. Humanoids will soon be capable of working alongside people in real workplaces, yet there is little independent research on how to deploy them safely, train workers, or develop appropriate regulation. This project will deliver the evidence, design principles, and workforce tools needed to guide their responsible introduction.

By combining expertise from engineering, design, health, and the social sciences, the Hub will develop frameworks that protect workers, uphold community values, and ensure technology serves public benefit. Industry partners will use the research to improve safety, efficiency and workforce resilience, while government and regulators will gain clear standards for accountability, privacy and safety. The outcomes will build sovereign capability, attract international collaboration, and position Australia as a trusted global leader in responsible humanoid robotics. This work directly contributes to national priorities in advanced manufacturing, care innovation and building a secure, resilient nation.

attributes.grant-summary: ARC Research Hub to Tackle Emerging Contaminants. This Hub aims to deliver fit-for-purpose, scalable and retrofit-ready technologies to address the challenge of emerging contaminants in the environment. The Hub expects to transform industry by developing innovative technologies, fast detection methods and advanced materials, supported by new business models. Expected outcomes include enhanced capabilities to secure a safe environment for both urban and rural communities, and improved health and wellbeing. The Hub will benefit Australia by opening up market opportunities for industry partners who are developing treatment technologies and sensors. The Hub will position Australia as a global leader in contaminant management and accelerate the national transition to a sustainable environment.

attributes.national-interest-test-statement: Exposure to various emerging contaminants (e.g., antimicrobial resistance, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), and micro/nanoplastics) has posed major threats to public health and ecosystem quality of Australia. The ARC Research Hub to Tackle Emerging Contaminants (ARC-TEC) aims to develop modular, scalable, and retrofit-ready technologies to address this critical challenge. Through developing advanced detection methods, innovative materials, and cutting-edge water/wastewater/biosolid treatment technologies, this Hub aims to efficiently achieve emerging contaminant removal and risk reduction with low chemical and energy demands. The Hub also aims to establish linkages between leading research groups and partner organisations to enhance the capabilities of Australian industry to address rapidly growing Australian and international challenges related to emerging contaminants in the environment. Our proposed business and practice model presents significant market opportunities and transformative potential for various stakeholders - including service and technology providers, manufacturing industry, and water industry - to become global leaders of novel detection and treatment technologies to address emerging contaminants. This ARC-TEC will bring significant economic, commercial, environmental, and social benefits to our Australian community, partner organisations, and end-users.

attributes.grant-summary:
ARC Training Centre for Animal Reproductive Biotechnologies. The ARC Training Centre for Animal Reproductive Biotechnologies (CARB) connects leading academics and industry to deliver innovations to Australian livestock sectors. CARB aims to train the next generation of industry-ready researchers and deliver solutions for cattle, sheep, pig, and horse reproduction, required for sustainable food production, and biodiversity conservation.  
Expected outcomes include a cohort of research students skilled in advanced reproductive biotechnologies, commercialisation, and adoption. By addressing critical skills shortages and targeting industry needs, CARB will drive higher fertility rates, on-farm efficiency, reduced emissions, faster genetic gain and strengthen Australia’s leadership in Agritech innovation.

attributes.national-interest-test-statement:
Australia’s livestock industries underpin regional jobs, exports and food security, yet productivity and sustainability are constrained by skills shortages and slow adoption of reproductive biotechnologies. The ARC Training Centre for Animal Reproductive Biotechnologies (CARB) will build sovereign capability by training an industry-embedded workforce able to develop novel reproductive solutions, adapt technologies to Australian conditions, and deploy existing tools in ways that transform breeding efficiency and sustainability. Co-led by UQ with the University of Sydney and the University of Newcastle, and co-designed with 17 partner organisations, CARB aims to translate assisted reproduction, semen and embryo technologies, and gene editing into cost-effective protocols suited to Australian systems. Outcomes include higher pregnancy rates, improved animal welfare, accelerated genetic gains, facilitated spread of climate-resilient traits, and strengthened market competitiveness & food security.

CARB’s integrated research, commercialisation and training programs align with Industrial Transformation Priorities in value-adding agriculture, enabling capabilities, and low-emissions technologies. By coupling frontier science with business model innovation, bio-entrepreneurship and adoption studies, CARB will deliver specialist workforce and technology pipeline that generates measurable economic, environmental and social benefits for producers, regional communities and biodiversity.

attributes.grant-summary: ARC Training Centre for Space Domain Awareness. A national research and training centre focused on space domain awareness will transform Australia’s ability to detect, track and characterise artificial and natural objects in Earth's space environment. The centre will advance and combine different sensing technologies and data-fusion methods, develop rapid hazard-assessment tools, and investigate the human and regulatory factors that support safe and responsible space operations. Intended outcomes include highly skilled graduates, new technologies for industry, and sovereign capability for managing satellites, space traffic, and space hazards. The anticipated benefits span national security, commercial growth, and broader community confidence in the reliable and sustainable use of space.

attributes.national-interest-test-statement:
Australia relies on satellites for communication, navigation, weather services, transport, emergency response and national security. Yet the space around Earth is becoming increasingly crowded with satellites, debris and natural objects. This creates growing risks to systems relied on by all Australians. Although Australia sits in one of the most valuable locations on the planet for observing space, it does not yet have a coordinated national program that brings together the research capability and skilled workforce needed to detect and understand these objects. At the same time, international partners are seeking Australian data because our unique southern-hemisphere coverage fills critical gaps in global space-tracking networks.

This new centre responds directly to this national opportunity and international need. It will advance new sensing technologies, real-time data-fusion methods and rapid hazard-assessment tools, while also examining the human and regulatory factors that support safe and responsible space operations. Benefits to Australians include more reliable satellite services, stronger national security, new commercial opportunities and the development of a highly skilled workforce for a fast-growing global industry.

To maximise adoption, the centre will work closely with industry, government and international partners, promote outcomes through national training and outreach, and release tools and methods where appropriate to deliver broad community benefit.

attributes.grant-summary: ARC Training Centre for Advanced Integrated Circuits. This Centre aims to transform Australia's technology sector industries by training a new generation of research and design leaders in mixed-signal advanced integrated circuits (ICs). The Centre expects to foster innovative research, co-developing next-generation technologies with industry, and provide unprecedented infrastructure support and training. Expected outcomes include new IC designs that will enable our digital future. This should provide significant benefits across a broad spectrum of industry sectors and applications including wireless and satellite communications, quantum systems, consumer electronics, and future medical devices. It will foster a skilled workforce of future leaders crucial for Australia’s economic development.
attributes.national-interest-test-statement: Australia risks being left behind in the integrated circuit (IC) revolution, with the global IC market projected to exceed USD 1 trillion by 2030, assuming continued research development breakthroughs. ICs are a key Enabling Capability for all advanced economies. This Centre will address industry’s growing need for skilled IC design engineers and research innovation. This will positively impact Australia’s economic resilience and national security. The expected outcomes of the Centre include a new cohort of industry-ready skilled IC leaders who will drive IC designs that are faster, smaller, and more energy-efficient, as well as new automated IC design processes and new licensed IP. They will deliver new technologies in wireless and satellite communications, quantum systems, consumer electronics, and future medical devices. This Centre will be unique in Australia and will especially support growth in small to medium enterprises (SMEs) and new entrants to the IC market. By prioritising design and IP creation, SMEs can capture the most profitable segment of the semiconductor value chain, without prohibitive infrastructure costs. Case studies from this Centre will be used to promote career opportunities to STEM graduates through public outreach events targeting schools and career fairs.

attributes.grant-summary: ARC Research Hub for AI-Powered Resilient Cities. This Research Hub will establish a world-leading capability in agentic artificial intelligence using multimodal geospatial data to enhance national resilience across transport, energy, and urban systems. It will enable real-time decision support and long-term scenario planning towards resilient cities. By integrating multimodal data, causal reasoning, and participatory planning, the Hub will create an end-to-end ecosystem that moves beyond prediction to reasoning, planning, and coordinated action, supporting real-time operational intelligence and long-horizon resilient planning. It will deliver significant economic, environmental, and societal benefits, safeguarding cities, communities, and critical systems against future disruptions.

attributes.national-interest-test-statement: This research project will help Australia better prepare for the unexpected by using artificial intelligence (AI) to understand and respond to complex, unpredictable challenges. The project aims to build intelligent systems that can detect and adapt to emerging threats, those we don’t yet know or fully understand. These “unknown unknowns” could include sudden infrastructure failures, unexpected shifts in urban mobility, or disruptions caused by new technologies or social behaviours. By analysing large volumes of real-world data, the AI models and agentic systems will support fast decision-making and long-term planning across transport, energy, and urban systems. This Hub unifies partners across academia, government, and industry to co-develop open, adaptive, and explainable AI systems that transform decision-making across transport, energy, and urban infrastructure. The Hub pioneers sovereign foundation models, simulation frameworks, and participatory design platforms that enable policy and operational coordination between agencies and sectors. The outcomes will benefit Australia economically by reducing the cost of reactive responses, socially by improving public safety and service delivery, and environmentally by enabling smarter infrastructure design. This research ensures public funds are invested in future-ready solutions that protect communities and help governments and industries stay ahead of change.

attributes.grant-summary: ARC Research Hub for Sustainable and Climate Smart Wastewater Solutions (SUCCESS) . Australia’s wastewater sector provides critical infrastructure that supports Australians' daily life. Yet, the already over-burdened sector lacks the capability to align with net-zero targets while providing reliable, cost-effective services. This Hub aims to use the challenge of greenhouse gas emissions as a catalyst to rethink entire interconnected wastewater systems. The Hub brings together universities, industry and community partners to develop new treatment solutions and digital tools that support better decisions, informing the upcoming once-in-a-generation opportunity to reshape Australia’s water systems. Hub innovations will deliver long-term benefits, including reduced pollution, lower energy use, and revitalised infrastructure.

attributes.national-interest-test-statement: Treating billions of litres of wastewater every day, our national utilities critically support public health, environmental protection and community liveability. However, Australia’s already over-burdened wastewater systems, which are large energy users and a major source of methane and nitrous oxide, are poorly equipped for meeting national net-zero targets. This Hub leverages an impressive collaboration of 22 universities, water utilities, technology companies and community partners to co-develop and deliver low-emissions, climate-smart urban water services through embedded mitigation in day-to-day operations, investment planning, and cross-sector interfaces with intelligent digital agents. Importantly, the Hub aligns precisely with major investment and planning cycles that Australian utilities will undertake over the next decade. Hub outputs will contribute directly to national climate resilience, economic productivity and community wellbeing. Hub innovations are expected to offer benefits to Australia, such as 10-25% savings to the sector on capital and operational/maintenance costs; adaptive controls to reduce N2O emissions by 20–40%; and local manufacturing and commercialisation opportunities for new technologies in growing domestic and international markets, such as the treatment solutions market expected to exceed $364B by 2029. The Hub will further deliver national capacity and help build a resilient workforce ready to support Australia’s net-zero transition.

attributes.grant-summary: ARC Research Hub for Recovering Energy and New Resources from Organics. The RENEW Organics Hub aims to create new ways to turn organic waste that currently goes to landfill into useful and safe products for farms, industry and clean energy. Many organic waste streams contain contaminants that make reuse difficult. The Hub will create safe, science-based methods to recover carbon, nutrients and energy by understanding contaminant behaviour and how they can be removed, neutralised or used safely. Working with industry, government and communities, it will deliver new processes, clear standards and trusted products that support jobs, protect the environment and advance Australia’s shift to a cleaner, circular, low-emission future while supporting key national priorities in waste, agriculture and clean energy.

attributes.national-interest-test-statement:
Australia generates over 14 million tonnes of organic waste each year, with 6.8 million tonnes still sent to landfill, producing methane emissions and losing valuable carbon, nutrients and energy. A major barrier to reuse is the presence of contaminants. Some contaminants could add value to new products, but only if their behaviour is understood and safely re-engineered. Australia lacks the contaminant-fate data, predictive models and risk frameworks needed to know when contaminants should be destroyed, immobilised or repurposed during thermal, chemical and biological processing.

The RENEW Organics Hub will address these gaps by creating Australia’s first contaminant-adaptive circular-manufacturing platform. Working with water utilities, councils, regulators, policy makers and industry, the Hub will generate new evidence, contaminant-fate models, scalability analysis and life-cycle data to support safe production of advanced carbon materials, fertilisers and clean fuels from complex wastes.

RENEW supports the National Waste Policy Action Plan, Circular Economy Framework and Net Zero targets. Outcomes will be promoted through government briefings, regulatory guidance, industry reports and co-designed public engagement programs. By providing the missing scientific evidence and translating it into policy and practice, RENEW will turn environmental liabilities into circular assets that reduce emissions, create regional jobs and strengthen Australia’s resource security.

attributes.grant-summary: ARC Research Hub: Geodynamic Pathways to Critical Resources (GeoPath) . The ARC Research Hub for Geodynamic Pathways to Critical Resources (GeoPath) will create a Virtual Earth for Resources to reveal how, where and why mineral systems form and persist through time. It will link deep Earth dynamics to surface processes and use AI to predict new mineral potential by combining plate reconstructions, mantle and landscape models, and data fusion tools. Working with industry, government and international partners, the Hub will reduce exploration risk and cost, support responsible resource discovery, and train a new generation of researchers skilled in geoscience, data analytics and decision science, strengthening Australia's resilience and supporting the global clean-energy transition.

attributes.national-interest-test-statement:
The ARC Research Hub for Geodynamic Pathways to Critical Resources (GeoPath) will enhance Australia's ability to discover and responsibly develop the minerals essential for a secure, low-carbon and strategically independent future. Copper and other critical minerals underpin renewable-energy technologies, defence capability, and advanced manufacturing, from batteries and satellites to telecommunications and electric vehicles. Yet discovery rates are falling as near-surface deposits are exhausted. GeoPath will combine deep-Earth modelling, surface-process simulations and artificial intelligence to predict where new resources are most likely to occur, reducing exploration risk, cost and environmental impact.

The Hub will unite Australian universities, government agencies and industry partners to create a national "Virtual Earth for Resources" -- an open, digital framework for predictive geoscience that connects deep-time Earth processes to modern exploration. This collaboration will position Australia as a global leader in responsible resource discovery, strengthen critical-minerals supply chains, and build sovereign capability vital for energy and defence security. GeoPath will also train a new generation of researchers skilled in geoscience, data analytics and decision science, expanding national expertise and diversity. The outcomes will advance national priorities on the net-zero transition, economic resilience, and the protection of Australia’s strategic interests.

attributes.grant-summary: ARC Training Centre for AI Governance, Oversight and Assurance. This ARC Training Centre for AI Governance, Oversight and Assurance aims to train a specialised workforce and advance safe, secure and privacy-preserving AI in critical sectors. Its significance lies in addressing Australia’s need for trustworthy AI and expertise in governance, assurance, certification and human-AI teaming. Expected outcomes include practical frameworks, tools and testbeds for transparent, compliant and resilient AI. The Centre will benefit partners through safer deployment and reduced systemic risk and its research impact will position Australia as a leader in responsible, standards-aligned, sovereign AI technologies.
attributes.national-interest-test-statement:
Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly being adopted everywhere including critical sectors such as defence, healthcare and Finance, where reliability and safety are paramount. However, Australia currently lacks the frameworks, tools, and skilled workforce needed to ensure these AI systems can be tested, certified, and deployed with confidence.
This ARC Training Centre for AI Governance, Oversight and Assurance will address this gap by developing practical methods to translate regulatory and safety requirements into technical processes that organisations can apply in real-world settings. Through collaboration with industry, government, and regulators, the Centre will create controlled test environments, assurance tools, and national frameworks that enable AI to be responsibly operationalised in high-stakes applications.
By building sovereign capability and training workforce who can bridge technology, safety, and regulation, the Centre will strengthen Australia’s ability to deploy advanced AI systems safely and at scale. These outcomes will enhance the performance and resilience of key national sectors, reduce risks from AI failure or misuse, and support innovation and productivity across the economy.

attributes.grant-summary: A novel integrated framework to study bacterial metabolism . This project will decipher how bacteria maintain metabolic homeostasis. Using an integrated approach that combines insights from enzyme chemistry with multi-omics datasets, it will study how bacteria regulate nutrient use to balance energy production and biosynthesis under changing conditions. The outcomes will include textbook-level knowledge of bacterial metabolism, revealing weak points in the metabolic network, and allowing us to explain and predict how bacteria adapt to nutrient stress. This innovative approach will set a new standard for linking how enzymes work with how cells behave. In the long term, the insights will inform antibiotic development and microbial engineering, strengthening Australia’s health and biotech capabilities.
attributes.national-interest-test-statement: Bacteria are essential to life on Earth, sustaining ecosystems, driving industrial processes and affecting human health. However, we still know very little about how bacteria control the use of nutrients that keep them alive. This lack of understanding limits our ability to harness their potential and manage their risks. This project will address this gap by uncovering how the bacteria that cause tuberculosis manage nutrient allocation and use under changing conditions. Understanding these processes will help Australia tackle challenges across multiple sectors. In health, it could lead to new strategies for treating infections such as tuberculosis, which disproportionately affects indigenous and migrant communities. In agriculture, it could contribute to controlling tuberculosis affecting livestock, potentially benefiting animal health, improving farming productivity and supporting an industry vital to Australia. In biotechnology, potential advances include sustainable manufacturing by improving microbial systems for water treatment, waste recycling and bio-based manufacturing. This project will also provide world-class training to the next generation of scientists. The results will be shared beyond academia through partnerships with industry, open-access data and public engagement. It will strengthen Australia’s capabilities in health, sustainability and biotechnology, while deepening our understanding of the fundamental biology that underpins these national priorities.

attributes.grant-summary: Climate change of the future constrained by the deep past. Future projections of climate change are similar to greenhouse conditions that the Earth last experienced more than 5 million years ago. These past greenhouse worlds had strong polar warming, which is not accurately reproduced by climate models. This project aims to improve simulations of past climate change that represent analogues of future climate change under medium and high emissions scenarios. Expected outcomes include improved paleoclimate reconstructions, more accurate polar warming and ocean circulation, and better constraints on future climate change. These outcomes should improve Australia’s capacity in climate modelling, and an improved understanding of cloud radiative forcing in past and future climates.
attributes.national-interest-test-statement: Climate change is one of Australia's most significant challenges, which affects our environment, health, economy and security. We rely on climate model projections to give accurate estimates of our long-term future, so that we can plan for, mitigate and adapt to future climate scenarios and their impact on society. Climate models are generally tested and tuned against historical observations of climate and weather. This means that they are not as well-tested or as accurate when compared with long-term geological records. However, future climate change scenarios are likely to resemble warm climates of the past, meaning it is crucial to be able to accurately explain and model past warm climates to give confidence in future projections. This project is expected to improve our understanding of past warm climates, especially in modelling the strong polar warming that is found in geological records. These outcomes will help to better understand future climate change, and the impact of enhanced polar warming on the ice sheets.

attributes.grant-summary: Nitrate-to-Ammonia Conversion for Circular Nitrogen Management. This project aims to develop a biological-chemical process to transform nitrate, a widespread pollutant, into valuable ammonia. Ammonia plays a vital role in food production and is increasingly recognised as a potential clean fuel. The project will investigate the microbial mechanisms driving nitrate-to-ammonia conversion and design an integrated treatment system to recover ammonia from nitrate-laden waste streams. Expected outcomes include uncovering fundamental microbial mechanisms and developing an innovative biochemical process for green ammonia recovery, with reduced nitrate pollution. The benefits include reduced environmental impacts and new opportunities for circular economy practices in agriculture, energy and the environment.
attributes.national-interest-test-statement: Ammonia is one of the most important chemicals in Australia’s economy, underpinning agriculture and increasingly recognised as a potential clean fuel in the energy sector. However, almost all ammonia today is produced by the Haber–Bosch process, which is highly energy-intensive and contributes substantially to global carbon dioxide emissions. At the same time, nitrate pollution from agriculture, industry, and wastewater poses ongoing risks to Australia’s waterways, ecosystems, and public health. This project directly addresses these two challenges by creating a new pathway to recover green ammonia from nitrate waste streams. The process will transform nitrate, currently managed as a costly pollutant, into a valuable ammonia product. If successful, the technology will reduce energy consumption, lower greenhouse gas emissions, and support Australia’s transition to a circular economy. It will also help reduce the environmental and social impacts of nitrate pollution, benefiting communities by protecting water quality. To maximise real-world impact, research outcomes will be promoted through industry partners, government agencies, and water utilities. Public communication will include workshops, demonstration projects, and outreach through media and community engagement programs. These activities will enhance awareness, accelerate technology translation, and support adoption by sectors critical to Australia’s clean energy and environmental sustainability goals.

attributes.grant-summary: Climate risks of a slowdown in Southern Ocean heat and carbon uptake. The Southern Ocean absorbs much of the excess heat and carbon released by human activity, slowing atmospheric warming and moderating extreme weather. However, there is a risk these ocean sinks of heat and carbon are not secure and could slow down as the ocean warms and becomes more acidic. Climate model projections are highly uncertain, which complicates adaptation planning. Using Australia’s next-generation ocean model, this project will develop new fundamental understanding of the complex ocean processes that control how the Southern Ocean takes up and stores heat and carbon. This will deliver more reliable projections of future climate and sea level, informing Australia’s planning for climate adaptation and coastal resilience.
attributes.national-interest-test-statement:
The Southern Ocean absorbs much of the excess heat and carbon released by human activity, acting as a crucial buffer of climate change and slowing atmospheric warming. However, there is a risk that this buffering capacity may not be secure. As the ocean warms and becomes more acidic, its absorption of heat and carbon could slow down this century and amplify warming of the atmosphere. Reliable projections of future climate are essential for national planning, yet climate models differ widely in how much heat and carbon they predict the Southern Ocean will absorb. 
This project will use Australia’s next-generation ocean model to develop fundamental understanding of the processes that govern how the Southern Ocean takes up, stores, and releases heat and carbon. It will examine how circulation, mixing, and fine-scale flows interact to shape this storage, how long heat and carbon remain sequestered, and how these processes respond to future climate change. 
By reducing uncertainty in projections of climate and sea-level rise, the project will directly support Australia’s climate adaptation strategies and coastal resilience. This will benefit the many sectors of society reliant on accurate medium- and long-term projections, including critical infrastructure, cultural heritage and ecosystem services. Results will be translated and shared with community, industry and government stakeholders through animations, public talks and policy briefings.

attributes.grant-summary: New Photochemical Strategies for Chemical Synthesis. This project aims to discover new light-driven catalytic strategies for advanced chemical synthesis. By integrating photochemical activation with precisely engineered auxiliaries and transition-metal catalysts, this project will deliver new synthetic technologies that employ inexpensive, abundant chemical feedstock such as carboxylic acids and olefins to rapidly generate molecules of increasing complexity and value. Expected outcomes include transformative advances in how chemists approach the design and synthesis of complex molecules, supporting innovation in the agricultural, pharmaceutical and materials sectors, and the training of highly skilled research scientists that strengthen Australia’s capacity in synthesis and catalysis.
attributes.national-interest-test-statement: The chemical and pharmaceutical sectors are vital to Australia’s economy, contributing over $38 billion annually and supporting a large, highly skilled workforce. However, many existing manufacturing processes remain energy-intensive and environmentally unsustainable long term. This project will develop innovative catalytic technologies that harness renewable visible light to drive efficient and selective chemical transformations. These new methods will reduce costs, energy use, and waste generation across chemical synthesis and manufacturing programs. By enabling the design and synthesis of molecules that are inaccessible using existing technologies, this research will directly advance drug discovery, materials development, and chemical biology, facilitating the creation of compounds with novel properties and functions. These outcomes will drive innovation across the agrochemical, pharmaceutical, and materials sectors, providing cleaner, safer, and more sustainable routes to high-value chemicals. Engagement with industry and research partners throughout this project will ensure the rapid translation of new discoveries into commercially relevant applications. This Future Fellowship will also strengthen national research capability by training highly skilled scientists and consolidating Australia’s leadership in sustainable chemical synthesis and advanced manufacturing.

attributes.grant-summary: Market and Welfare Implications of Biased Beliefs. Markets work well when people read signals—prices, reviews, labels—correctly. This project aims to explain when and why people misread those signals, and how to fix it. The project expects to generate new knowledge by developing and experimentally testing behavioural models of how individuals form and update beliefs. Expected outcomes include new economic frameworks to quantify the impact of distorted beliefs for auctions, negotiations, and firm pricing. These frameworks should yield substantial economic and social benefits by providing new policy instruments to help markets convey information more accurately, such as quality certification standards and transparent advertising rules, thereby supporting fairer and more efficient markets.
attributes.national-interest-test-statement: This project examines how people form and update beliefs in everyday economic situations, and why they often misinterpret key signals like prices, product reviews, or labels. By combining behavioural insights with economic theory and experimental studies, it will pinpoint when these misread signals lead to problems in markets—such as paying too much at auctions, failing to reach a deal in negotiations, or undermining the value of product certifications. Understanding these belief errors is crucial as they can cost Australians money, reduce fair competition, and erode trust. For example, if consumers misunderstand a high price as a guarantee of quality or put too much faith in an online review, they might overpay or select the wrong product. The findings will help regulators like the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) and agencies such as the Australian Government's Behavioural Economics Team (BETA) craft stronger consumer protection policies and clearer pricing guidelines. Industry can also benefit by learning to present information in ways that consumers can easily understand, leading to more informed choices and less wasteful spending. Importantly, the project will develop simple, practical tools-—like improved product labels or clearer disclosure rules—to help people make better decisions. All results will be shared widely through workshops and open-access publications, ensuring policymakers, businesses, and the public can benefit from the findings.

attributes.grant-summary: Families, Housing Precarity and Generational Inequalities. This study explores how Australian family lives are being reshaped by the housing crisis. Family homelessness, housing precarity and constrained family and housing aspirations affect people of all ages, across generations. Implications for everyday family lives and family and housing coping strategies are under-explored as are wider impacts on society and the economy. This pioneering study uses longitudinal mixed methods, comparative analysis and co-design with lived experience experts to develop novel evidence about housing challenges facing diverse families, and explore solutions: finance, assistance and tenure options and dwelling alternatives. It will inform policy and industry change, leading international innovation in family housing.
attributes.national-interest-test-statement: More Australian families with children and groups such as older single women are at risk of homelessness. Strains from insecure housing appear at key points of family change: childbirth, caring, young adults leaving home, partnering, separation, and ageing. Across income levels, cultural backgrounds and regions, more families are finding housing aspirations unmet and generational life chances limited by housing precarity. They adapt in various ways, with unequal gender, generational and family impacts. The nexus between family life and housing is changing in ways that are not yet well understood. This Fellowship pioneers Australia’s first national mixed-method, longitudinal, and multi-scalar family–housing research program, bringing lifecourse and comparative insight to how evolving housing systems intersect with diverse family lives. It conceptualises and quantifies family-related housing precarity using longitudinal and novel survey data, analyses systems shaping family-housing interactions and illuminates family strategies and system adaptations emerging in response. Through co-production with lived-experience and cross-sector stakeholders, it will generate evidence-based innovation to help ensure the Australian Government’s $33 billion housing investment delivers equitable, diverse, and sustainable benefits—reducing inequalities, supporting social cohesion, and strengthening national wellbeing. Impact will be amplified via wide academic, community and media dissemination.

attributes.grant-summary: Spatially Reconfigurable Antenna Arrays for High-Speed 6G Wireless Networks. This project aims to advance sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks by leveraging revolutionary spatially reconfigurable antenna arrays. It focuses on establishing fundamental communication theory and developing pragmatic resource allocation strategies to maximise data rates. Current fixed-position antenna arrays cannot adapt to surging data demand, leaving networks congested and inefficient. The proposed innovations will deepen knowledge in high-speed communications, significantly improve network performance and reduce operational costs. Aligning with Australia’s List of Critical Technologies, the outcomes will strengthen Australia’s 6G industry, enhance productivity and support its leadership in information and communications technology.
attributes.national-interest-test-statement: Australia’s telecommunications industry is a cornerstone of the economy, generating tens of billions of dollars each year and supporting health, education, agriculture and business. Yet this industry faces a pressing challenge: mobile data traffic is expected to grow more than ninefold by 2030 compared with 2020, posing risks of network congestion, higher consumer costs and slower services. Today’s fixed-position antennas cannot adapt to this demand, leaving networks struggling to keep pace. This project addresses that gap by developing future 6G wireless networks powered by spatially reconfigurable antenna arrays. Unlike traditional antennas, these can reposition and reorient in real time, ensuring faster and more efficient wireless services. The outcomes will reduce operating costs for providers, support more affordable wireless connectivity for households, deliver consistent coverage to regional communities and strengthen Australia’s competitiveness in global information and communications technology markets. They will also enable transformative applications such as remote healthcare, precision farming and immersive education. To maximise national benefit, findings will be shared widely through public talks, media engagement and social platforms, alongside workshops with industry, government and community stakeholders. These pathways will accelerate adoption, attract investment and strengthen Australia’s position as a leader in sustainable, world-class 6G technologies.

attributes.grant-summary: A Unified Framework for Next-Generation High Density Power Converters. A key limitation in next-generation power electronics is the lack of a unified framework that integrates devices, passives, thermal management, EMI & control. This project aims to develop a multi-physics framework for next-generation power converters by combining circuit architectures, magnetics, thermal pathways, packaging &  control in one co-design flow. Expected outcomes include new knowledge from advanced modelling & benchmarking of electro-thermal & electromagnetic interactions, along with novel architectures, validated models & open benchmarking tools. This will enable compact, efficient, reliable converters for energy, transport, aerospace & digital infrastructure while enhancing Australia’s leadership in clean energy technologies.
attributes.national-interest-test-statement:
Australia’s shift to clean energy, electric vehicles, and advanced digital infrastructure relies on power converters that are efficient, compact, and reliable. However, current design methods are fragmented, making it difficult to create the next generation of converters needed for these technologies. This project will develop a new, unified approach to designing power converters, bringing together electrical, thermal, and magnetic aspects into a single, easy-to-use framework.

By making converter design faster, more accurate and more reliable, this research could help Australian industries—such as energy, transport, aerospace, and defence—reduce costs, improve competitiveness and support the transition to cleaner technologies. Environmentally, more efficient converters mean less energy waste and lower emissions, helping Australia meet its climate goals. Socially, the project could strengthen the resilience of our infrastructure, improve energy security, and create opportunities for training the next generation of skilled workers.

To ensure these benefits reach beyond academia, the project will share its tools and findings openly with industry, government, and the wider community. This includes developing user-friendly design tools, holding workshops and working with partners to encourage adoption and real-world impact. In this way, the project supports Australia’s national priorities for clean energy, advanced manufacturing, and a skilled workforce.

attributes.grant-summary: Transforming Portable Magnetic Resonance through Molecular Innovation. This project aims to solve the problem of low sensitivity in compact magnetic resonance instruments by developing new chemical strategies to enhance detection at low magnetic fields. It expects to generate new knowledge by designing molecules that improve signal strength, eliminating the need for powerful magnets and costly cooling systems. Expected outcomes include improved sensing of chemicals relevant in agriculture, environmental monitoring and manufacturing. This should provide significant benefits by improving the performance of compact, affordable instruments for detecting environmental contaminants and compounds used to verify product quality, supporting national priorities in environmental resilience and advanced manufacturing.
attributes.national-interest-test-statement:
This project will develop innovative chemical methods to dramatically enhance the sensitivity of magnetic resonance, the technology behind MRI and chemical sensors. It will enable devices to be smaller, cheaper, and more portable by boosting performance at low magnetic fields, which are safer and more affordable but currently less sensitive.
Traditional scanners are large, expensive, and require special cooling, limiting their use in environmental monitoring, quality assurance, and rural healthcare. This research addresses that gap by enhancing compact, low-field devices for improved detection of soil and water contaminants, monitoring chemical residues in agriculture, manufacturing and forensics, and supporting medical imaging in remote and emergency settings.
The project will strengthen Australia’s capacity to deliver more versatile diagnostic tools, improved food and water monitoring and enhanced manufacturing efficiency, aligning with national priorities in health, environmental resilience, and advanced manufacturing. By reducing reliance on imported helium used in traditional scanners, it will also bolster sovereign capability and supply chain resilience.
Research translation will be driven by strategic engagement with end-users across agriculture, environmental monitoring, and manufacturing. Innovations will be communicated through sector-specific forums and tested in real-world conditions via collaborative partnerships, ensuring relevance, uptake and long-term impact.
